paper.title_en: Optimal four-copy detection of the three-tangle and its fault-tolerant cost
paper.abstract_en: The three-tangle, $τ_3$, is a measure of genuine tripartite entanglement that distinguishes GHZ-type from W-type entanglement in pure three-qubit states. Here, we identify the statistically optimal one-sided four-copy detector of the three-tangle and study its implementation cost. The optimal detector has click probability $τ_3^2/48$, while previous four-copy constructions achieve $τ_3^2/256$ and therefore require asymptotically $16/3$ times as many experimental repetitions. Using the representation-theoretic structure of the problem, we construct an ancilla-free implementation of the optimal detector using 15 CNOT gates, together with an 11-CNOT detector with click probability $τ_3^2/96$. These results reveal a tradeoff between statistical efficiency and implementation cost, since reducing the number of repetitions requires increasingly expensive circuits. We then show that this tradeoff persists once the circuits are encoded. In a fully fault-tolerant setting, the increased click probability comes with a substantial non-Clifford synthesis cost, while an early fault-tolerant implementation based on $T$ gates and STAR rotations reduces this overhead at the expense of additional encoded resources. We quantify these costs using both the Steane and $[[8,3,2]]$ codes, providing explicit resource estimates for implementing the optimal detector across different computational regimes.
